newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis lashed out at his ministers yesterday for their lack of coordination and their squabbling. Speaking to ruling party PASOK MPs, a dissatisfied Simitis said the government's profile was "grey" and that there were delays in the implementation of policies.

--Yesterday's low-key beginning to the farmers' second round of protests has bred hope that the mobilisations this time will be less disruptive. Both sides avoided antagonising the other, with farmers distributing flowers to police forces in the city of Karditsa.

--Teacher, however, are continuing the second week of their strike into the next, rejecting proposals from Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis. Also on strike next week are primary school and kindergarten teachers.

--The Greek economy is entering a period of unforeseen rapid de-escalation of inflation, laying the ground for a similar fall in interest rates and increased growth. Latest figures show that inflation may fall below 7.0 percent this month and, at worst, will end at 7.1 percent.

--There are warnings from Bonn that it will not allow Athens to hinder the expansion of the European Union to ensure the inclusion of Cyprus. "Do not over-estimate our patience," a German official is reported to have said.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Striking teachers have failed Education Minister Arsenis on his maths. The union, OLME, has decided to continue and expand strike action.

--Farmers' protests may have got off to a slow start yesterday but today is expected to expand with hundreds of police officers guarding public buildings targeted by the farmers. A "warm reception" is being planned for Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas in Thessaloniki - to open the Agrotica trade fair - today.
--Russian foreign ministry officials are expected in Athens from Ankara today, continuing Moscow's initiative on Cyprus.

--Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos said yesterday that it was not possible for construction work on the Goulandris Museum of Modern Art to continue following the discovery of the ruins of the Lyceum.
TA NEA

--A nationwide poll has shown 80 percent of Greeks believe the farmers to be justified in their demands but with only 32 percent approving of road blocks. The poll was taken in mid-December, at the height of the 25-day blockade.
--Monthly increases of between 8.2-16.9 percent have failed to convince teachers to return to their classrooms. Schools will remain shut for a third week.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--Bluntly-spoken Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos has said he will mobilise all forces against the farmers - even brand-new Chinook helicopters - to ensure the law is upheld during farmers' protests.
ETHNOS

--Farmers may have distributed flowers to police officers in Karditsa yesterday a la Belgrade protestors but Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas can expect to be greeted like a Milosevic when he arrives in Thessaloniki tonight.
--Experts are conducting checks on school buildings following the collapse of a schoolroom instrong winds earlier this week.
--A 90-year-old farmer has donated his savings of one million drachmas to the armed forces to buy "one or two gunboats". --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
